question: A manager tells staff to draft sensitive client material on their own personal Claude accounts rather than on the company's Claude for Work account, because "the Work account trains on our chats". What is the accurate correction?
options: A) The advice is right, but only for staff who have already switched model improvement off on their own accounts.
B) The advice is right, because business accounts always carry much broader training permissions than personal ones do.
C) The advice makes no difference, because the training rules are identical on personal and on business accounts.
D) The advice has the risk backwards, since a training choice exists on personal accounts but not on the Work account.
correct_answers: D) The advice has the risk backwards, since a training choice exists on personal accounts but not on the Work account.
explanations: A personal privacy setting does not make a personal account the appropriate home for company material.
Business plans do not grant broader training permissions; the default runs in the opposite direction.
The consumer and the commercial rules are different, which is precisely what the manager has confused.

Correct. Commercial products do not train on inputs and outputs by default, while consumer accounts carry a personal model improvement choice, so moving the work to a personal account increases exposure.
